question: Which of the following sites are used for storage of waste products in plants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Old xylem**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Old xylem tissue, after it has lost its primary function of conducting water and minerals, can be used for storage of waste products in plants.
 
• These waste products, also known as **secondary metabolites**, include substances like tannins, alkaloids, and pigments.
 
• These compounds are often stored in the heartwood of trees, which is the older, darker part of the trunk.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guard cells:**

 
 
• These are specialized cells found in the epidermis of leaves.
 
• They regulate the opening and closing of stomata, which are tiny pores on the surface of leaves. They do not store waste products.
 
 
 
• **Root hairs:**
 
 
• **​** These are tiny projections on the surface of root cells that increase the surface area for absorption of water and minerals.
 
• They do not store waste products.
 
 
 
• **Phloem fibers:**
 
 
• **​** These are elongated cells found in the phloem tissue of plants.
 
• They provide structural support and transport organic nutrients.
 
• They do not store waste products.
